title: Boss: the Friday deploy
summary: The Lighthouse Tickets API goes out on Friday. Review fixes from the on-call log: blocking calls, an N+1 page and edits that overwrite each other.

steps.title: The Friday deploy
body: The Lighthouse Tickets API ships on Friday, before the Saturday on-sale. Last week's on-call notes:
19:02  p99 latency 9 s on GET /events, thread pool starvation warnings, CPU 15 %
19:05  DBA: "a query with no tag runs 40k times a minute, which endpoint is it?"
19:20  GET /bookings: 1 + 4,800 SQL commands per request in the dev log
19:41  support: two agents edited the same booking, the second silently overwrote the first
Three fixes, one per step. Every handler should end up async with the request's `CancellationToken`.

steps.title: Step 1: async, untracked and tagged
prompt: `GET /events` (sorted by `StartsAt`) and `GET /events/{id}` (404 if missing) block threads and cannot be found in the DBA's tools. Rewrite both:
- async handlers taking `CancellationToken ct`, with `ToListAsync(ct)` and `FirstOrDefaultAsync(ct)`;

The API has `Event` (`Id`, `Name`, `StartsAt`, `Bookings`) and `Booking` (`Id`, `EventId`, `Event`, `Customer`, `Note`, and `Version` as a `[ConcurrencyCheck]` token). The POST endpoints that the tests use to create data are given. **Run checks** starts your server and calls it.
template: public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
await http.PostAsJsonAsync("/events", new { name = "The Gannets", startsAt = "2026-12-04 20:00" });
await http.PostAsJsonAsync("/events", new { name = "Foghorn Choir", startsAt = "2026-12-12 18:00" });
await http.PostAsJsonAsync("/bookings", new { eventId = dojoE, customer = dojoC, note = "" });
Dojo.Eq("GET /events, soonest first", "The Gannets|Saltmarsh|Foghorn Choir", Each(dojoList, "name"));
Dojo.Check("...tagged GET /events in the SQL", dojoSql.StartsWith("-- GET /events"), "the SQL starts with: " + dojoSql.Split('\n')[0]);
static string Each(JsonElement json, string prop) =>
json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array ? string.Join("|", json.EnumerateArray().Select(x => DojoWeb.Prop(x, prop))) : "(not an array)";
if (e.Value is CommandExecutedEventData d) lock (Log) Log.Add(d.Command.CommandText);

require.message: Tags the list query with TagWith

hints: Each handler becomes `async (..., TicketsDb db, CancellationToken ct) => await ...`.

steps.title: Step 2: the bookings page
prompt: `GET /bookings` returns every booking as `BookingRow(Id, Customer, EventName)`, by id. The dev log shows one query for the bookings and then one `SELECT ... FROM "Events" WHERE "e"."Id" = @b_EventId` per booking.
Make it **one** SQL command whatever the number of bookings: project through the `Event` navigation. Keep `ToListAsync(ct)`.

The API has `Event` (`Id`, `Name`, `StartsAt`, `Bookings`) and `Booking` (`Id`, `EventId`, `Event`, `Customer`, `Note`, and `Version` as a `[ConcurrencyCheck]` token). The POST endpoints that the tests use to create data are given. **Run checks** starts your server and calls it.
template: public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
await http.PostAsJsonAsync("/events", new { name = "The Gannets", startsAt = "2026-12-04 20:00" });
await http.PostAsJsonAsync("/events", new { name = "Foghorn Choir", startsAt = "2026-12-12 18:00" });
await http.PostAsJsonAsync("/bookings", new { eventId = dojoE, customer = dojoC, note = "" });
Dojo.Eq("...with event names", "The Gannets|Saltmarsh|Foghorn Choir|The Gannets", Each(dojoRows, "eventName"));
Dojo.Check("...in one SQL command", dojoCount == 1, $"it ran {dojoCount} commands");
static string Each(JsonElement json, string prop) =>
json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array ? string.Join("|", json.EnumerateArray().Select(x => DojoWeb.Prop(x, prop))) : "(not an array)";
if (e.Value is CommandExecutedEventData d) lock (Log) Log.Add(d.Command.CommandText);
hints: Select straight into the record: `.Select(b => new BookingRow(b.Id, b.Customer, b.Event!.Name))`.

steps.title: Step 3: edits that do not overwrite
prompt: `PUT /bookings/{id}` takes `{ "note": "...", "version": 1 }` (the version the agent's screen loaded) and saves it whatever the version. Fix it:
- compare with the **client's** version (`OriginalValue = edit.Version`), and set `Version = edit.Version + 1`;
- on `DbUpdateConcurrencyException`: **409** with a body that includes **`currentVersion`**, the version now in the database (`ex.Entries[0].GetDatabaseValuesAsync(ct)`), so the screen can reload;
- 404 for an unknown booking, as now.

The API has `Event` (`Id`, `Name`, `StartsAt`, `Bookings`) and `Booking` (`Id`, `EventId`, `Event`, `Customer`, `Note`, and `Version` as a `[ConcurrencyCheck]` token). The POST endpoints that the tests use to create data are given. **Run checks** starts your server and calls it.
template: public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
await http.PostAsJsonAsync("/events", new { name = "The Gannets", startsAt = "2026-12-04 20:00" });
await http.PostAsJsonAsync("/events", new { name = "Foghorn Choir", startsAt = "2026-12-12 18:00" });
await http.PostAsJsonAsync("/bookings", new { eventId = dojoE, customer = dojoC, note = "" });
var dojoOk = await http.PutAsJsonAsync("/bookings/2", new { note = "wheelchair space", version = 1 });
DojoWeb.Status("a save with the loaded version responds 200", 200, dojoOk);
var dojoStale = await http.PutAsJsonAsync("/bookings/2", new { note = "front row", version = 1 });
var dojoAgain = await http.PutAsJsonAsync("/bookings/2", new { note = "front row", version = 2 });
Dojo.Eq("after reloading, the save works and returns version 3", "3", DojoWeb.Prop(await DojoWeb.Json(dojoAgain), "version"));
DojoWeb.Status("PUT /bookings/9 responds 404", 404, await http.PutAsJsonAsync("/bookings/9", new { note = "x", version = 1 }));
static string Each(JsonElement json, string prop) =>
json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array ? string.Join("|", json.EnumerateArray().Select(x => DojoWeb.Prop(x, prop))) : "(not an array)";
if (e.Value is CommandExecutedEventData d) lock (Log) Log.Add(d.Command.CommandText);

require.message: Reads the current values on conflict

hints: Copy the client's version into `db.Entry(booking).Property(b => b.Version).OriginalValue` before saving.
In the catch: `var current = await ex.Entries[0].GetDatabaseValuesAsync(ct);` then `current?.GetValue<int>("Version")`.
steps.explain: Ship it. Next week's on-call log should show tagged queries, one command per page, and 409s instead of silent overwrites.
